summary: Chain-of-Symbol prompting replaces verbose natural-language reasoning traces with compact symbolic intermediate representations, especially for structured spatial reasoning tasks.
why_it_matters: It is relevant to planning and reasoning in the vault because it shows that smaller, more structured intermediate representations can improve both reasoning quality and efficiency.
method_setup: The paper converts chain-of-thought examples into symbolic forms for spatial planning and reasoning tasks such as Brick World, navigation, and manipulation, then compares symbolic prompting with natural-language CoT across models.
key_claims: Symbolic intermediate representations can outperform natural-language CoT on structured spatial tasks.
Compact symbolic reasoning can cut token use substantially while improving accuracy.
Larger models appear better able to benefit from abstract symbolic reasoning traces.
limitations: The benefits are demonstrated mainly on spatially structured reasoning tasks.
The prompting style depends on manually designed symbolic formats and examples.
